newsitem.title: USA: Latin America economies to grow 4.5 pct in '97 - IADB.
newsitem.headline: Latin America economies to grow 4.5 pct in '97 - IADB.

text.p: Latin America and the Caribbean will grow by at least 4.5 percent this year, an improvement over 1996 when the region's economies grew 3.1 percent, the Inter-American Development Bank said on Monday.
The faster overall growth reflects continued recovery from the recessions that hit Mexico and Argentina in 1995, the IADB said in its annual report.

"The growth projection for this year is about 4.5 percent, and it could be higher," Bank president Enrique Iglesias told reporters a week ago before leaving for the board of governors meeting in Barcelona, Spain.
But he said the economic growth was not enough to reduce unemployment, which appeared to have increased in the region.
Bank economists said the preliminary 1996 growth figure of 3.1 percent was being revised upwards to about 3.5 percent.
Average inflation, however, fell to 11 percent in 1996 from 13 percent the year before and was the lowest rate since 1977.
Last year also saw a major recovery in private capital inflows to the region, rising sharply from 1995 to recover levels of investment that existed prior to the Mexican crisis.
Iglesias said IADB lending had focused on social projects and reform in 1996, emphasising urban development, public health and education.
